 Judgment

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.1051/2018 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kozhikode (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 31/01/2020.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.
2. The claim petitioners are the father, mother and younger sister respectively of deceased Nithin.

According to the claim petitioners, on 17/08/2017 at about 05:30 a.m., while the deceased was crossing the road in front of SBI, Pantheerankavu, 2025:KER:39345 car bearing registration no.KL-55-E-2854 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked down him causing fatal injuries to which he succumbed.
Dharmarajan.M.C vs Abdul Razaq.

P on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199055459/
2 3.
The first respondent driver and the second respondent owner filed written statement disputing negligence on the part of the first respondent.
The accident occurred due to the carelessness on the part of deceased while crossing the road.
The vehicle was duly insured with the third respondent at the time of the accident.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement disputing the negligence of the first respondent.
The age and injuries sustained to the deceased were disputed.
The amount of compensation claimed was contended to be excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, PWs.1 and 2 were examined and Exts.A1 to A10 were marked on the side of the claim petitioners.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced by the respondents.

The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the first respondent-driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 19,74,500/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.

Aggrieved by the Award,
the claim petitioners have come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads are challenged by the claim petitioners - Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim 2025:KER:39345 petitioners that the deceased, a bachelor, aged 24 years was a tipper lorry driver and was earning about 25,000/- to 30,000/- per month.
In order to substantiate the said allegation, the claim petitioners relied on Ext.A9 and the testimony of PW2.

However, the Tribunal fixed the monthly income at 12,000/- per month, which is challenged by the learned counsel for the claim petitioners who submits that in the light of the evidence adduced, the amount fixed is too low.
The fact that the deceased was a driver is established by Ext.A9 driving licence.
Hence in these circumstances and relying on the dictum in Manusha Sreekumar v. The United India Insurance Co.Ltd., (2022) 17 SCC 321, I find that the notional income can be fixed at 16,600/-.

 Total Limited to 19,74,400/-
 50,00,000/- Round off to 26,69,920/-

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 6,95,420/- (total compensation 26,69,920/- that is, 19,74,500/-
granted by the Tribunal + 6,95,420/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization 2025:KER:39345 and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurance company is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
